**BOOK I — THE HOUSE OF MENDERS · Chapter 4 — Old Mercy**

- **Where:** Saint Ysolde's, the House of Menders; on the floor of the infirmary hall by the undercroft door, beside Hollis; the Prior standing off; Maelis gone up the row.
- **The quest:** *The List.* The Confessors have come for the Faithless at Saint Ysolde's with a list: Darrow first, Hollis second. The named are to be taken down the Steps to the Oathspire and made to kneel where everyone can watch, which would say the Ninth drowned for its own bad faith, and would tear the thread in Darrow's knee. What stands between them and the hall is Old Mercy, the sanctuary bell: while it rings at dawn and dusk, no blade passes the gate and no name under it is taken down against its will. Miss one ringing and the law lapses till the next, and Sister Pell, who rings it, is very old. At the gate, Confessor Ivo Marrant read his names at the bars, and two of his men came through the wicket before the bell rang, late. Now five grey cloaks are camped on the lower terrace below the gate, and the sixth holds the winch-house, the cage and Rae's cart, so the road is theirs. Marrant's price: the Captain of the Ninth comes down and kneels, and the rest of the paper goes back in his cloak. Darrow went to the bars and gave him his name and his face. Marrant says he will wait.
- **What Darrow is fighting right now:** The soft season, and the waiting. The knee is held and still soft. Benedek lies Hollowed in the Grey Cot, and nobody passed in the night; the Confessor's word for it, ember witchcraft, is in the hall now, and the hall wants a hand to fit it. Under it is the thing he has said only to Maelis: a lad who cannot answer has no will for the bell to keep.
- **With him:** Maelis Vorne (Gone up the row. She will not carry it to the Prior and will not stand beside him when he does.) · Ser Hollis Garrow (On the floor at the stair head with the lad's blanket pulled straight, sending for the novice who feeds the far cots.) · Wren Ashdown (Standing at the linen press with her hand on the slab of mortar, white, counting something under her breath that nobody asked for.)
- **Also here:** Ser Aldric Vane (Wrote again from Calden, before the list was read: Calden says the Ninth broke faith when its captain turned out of the line for one of his…) · Ser Benedek Orrin (Said his oath at the noon bell with Hollis's hand round his; the frost on his mouth neither grew nor melted.) · Confessor Ivo Marrant (Came to the bars at the dawn bell to ask for the Captain's answer, read it at the gate, thanked him for his candour, and sent it down the S…) · Mother Ione (Watched Maelis go, then Darrow, and still asked nothing.) · Sister Pell (Rang the hours through the night and came down between every bell to sit by the undercroft door; heard nothing come or go; told Hollis she…)
- **The tales:** Tale 1 — Quickstep (1 of 3 told)
- **Against him:** The black sliver stays in the wall under the row, its lid broken off and known; the Prior has not been told; Maelis has walked away from it; his right hand is out of use for a week.
- **Next:** The far cots' keepers tonight; the Prior after.
- **Open choice:** none.
